E[S_obs]=∑_k θ/k [1-f^k]=θ a_n - θ∑_k f^k/k,
∑_k f^k/k = -log(1-f)=O(1)<∞,
a_n=∑_{k=1}^{2n-1}1/k ~ log n →∞.

f^{2np}→0. Up to the usual VCF ascertainment to variable sites, Watterson θ_W=S/a_n is asymptotically recovered; the O(1) loss θ∑f^k/k is o(a_n) and vanishes relatively as n→∞.

PUBLIC RESPONSE: B. Only pi is persistently biased on the ascertained VCF site set; θW is first order asymptotically robust under MCAR loss + reference fill-in.

Let f>0 be the per haplotype per site probability that a true derived call is filtered and r=1-f the retention probability, and let the imputed allele be Y = X B with B ~ Bern(r). On the union VCF site set every site is truly segregating, p>0.

* Frequency information.
E[ p̂ | p ] = r p < p.  The reference allele is never created.
For a site
Pr{Yi ≠ Yj}=2 r p[1- r p] < 2p(1-p)
so
E[ π̂_i | p ] = 2 r p[1- r p] < 2p(1-p)  ∀0<p<1,
and with p≪1 E[π̂_i]≈2 r p. Hence

E[π̂] = E_p[2 r p(1-r p)] < E_p[2p(1-p)] = π_true

and the r-attenuation of the derived allele frequency persists as n→∞. The pairwise-difference average is systematically depressed by the reference imputation, i.e. classic missing-as-reference frequency bias.

* Presence/absence information.
A true site with k=2np>0 derived copies is scored monomorphic after imputation iff all k copies are filtered,
Pr{ site lost | k } = f^{k},  Pr{ site segregating | k}=1-f^{k}.
For any fixed p>0, f^{k}=f^{2np}→0 as n→∞. With the stated “no completely missing SNV across all samples’’ the analysed site set is the true segregating set S_T. Under infinite sites E[N_k]=θ/k,

E[S_obs]= Σ_k θ/k [1-f^{k}] = θ a_n - θ Σ_k f^{k}/k,
Σ_k f^{k}/k = -log(1-f)=O(1),
a_n = Σ_{1}^{2n-1}1/k ~ log n →∞.

Hence
θ̂_W^obs = S_obs/a_n = θ[1 - Σ f^{k}/k / a_n] → θ in probability,
S_obs → S_true w.h.p. The O(1) absolute loss θ Σ f^{k}/k is o(a_n); the relative bias of Watterson vanishes as n→∞.

The usual upward VCF ascertainment to variable sites is common to both statistics and is not created by the imputation step. Conditional on the VCF site set the segregating-site count, and therefore θW, is asymptotically recovered by random allele-independent loss with reference fill-in, whereas the frequency-weighted π remains permanently depressed by the r thinning of derived allele frequencies. In finite n both are mildly downward biased by the f^{k} tail, the relative bias of θW being O(1/log n)→0, which is the usual S-robust vs π-sensitive behaviour.

Let f>0 be the per-haplotype filtering probability and r=1-f the retention probability for a true derived copy. On a true derived frequency p>0

E[ p̂ | p ] = r p < p

because a derived copy is seen only when it survives the filter and a reference copy is never turned into derived. Hence for every site

E[ 2 p̂(1-p̂) | p ] = 2 r p [1 - r p] < 2 p (1-p)

and

E[ π̂ ] = E_p[ 2 r p (1- r p) ] < E_p[ 2 p (1-p) ] = π_true .

The r attenuation of the observed allele frequency persists for every n, so nucleotide diversity is persistently downward shifted by the imputation. That part is uncontroversial.

The same thinning changes the segregating-site count that enters Watterson. A site with k true derived copies in the 2n haplotypes is seen as segregating after imputation iff at least one of those k copies survives filtering,

Pr{ site segregating | k } = 1 - f^k .

On the infinite-sites spectrum E[N_k]=θ/k this gives

E[ S_obs ] = Σ_k θ/k [1 - f^k] = θ a_n - θ Σ_k f^k/k ,

a_n = Σ_{k=1}^{2n-1} 1/k ,  Σ_k f^k/k = -log(1-f) >0 .

So the expected number of segregating sites on the union VCF set is smaller than the true number by the constant θ Σ f^k/k. The “no completely missing SNV across all samples’’ condition is a property of the pre-filter union; after sample-specific deletion plus reference imputation a site can be imputed as reference/reference in every haplotype and become monomorphic in the final alignment.

Hence E[ S_obs ] < S_true for every finite n, and

E[ θ̂_W^obs ] = E[ S_obs ]/a_n = θ [1 - (-log(1-f))/a_n ] < θ .

The relative bias (-log(1-f))/a_n →0 as a_n ~ log n →∞, i.e. for fixed p>0, f^{2np} →0, so the bias of S/a_n can be made arbitrarily small. That is an asymptotic relative statement. The question is about the calculation that is actually performed with an arbitrarily large but finite number of phased samples and a substantial minority per-sample filter. In that operational setting the expectation of S, and therefore of θ_W = S/a_n, is strictly below its true value on the ascertained VCF site set, because rare sites are lost with probability f^k>0 and are then reference-imputed away.

Thus the reference imputation makes the constructed alignments systematically reference-enriched: the frequency-weighted average π is attenuated by the r factor, and the presence/absence count S is under-counted by the f^k loss. Conditional on the VCF ascertained set both estimators are downward biased in expectation, with the familiar O(1) loss in S being the finite-sample form that the asymptotic “θ_W is recovered’’ argument sweeps under the o(log n) rug. That is the both-biased operational conclusion for missing-as-reference imputation.

<E_{p}[2p(1-p)]=\pi_{true}$,

Presence/absence is different.  With $k_{n}=2np$ true derived copies

and a site is seen as segregating iff $K_{o}>0$ with $K_{o}\mid k\sim

 =\theta\Bigl[1-\frac{\sum f^{k}/k}{a_{n}}\Bigr]\xrightarrow{p}\theta$

derived copies are filtered, $f^{k_{n}}$, goes to zero with $n$ and

loss $\theta\sum f^{k}/k$ is $o(a_{n})$, i.e. a finite-sample

count and therefore Watterson’s $\theta_{W}$ is first order robust to

The reference fill-in is a one-way enrichment for the reference allele and that enrichment is systematic on the actual alignments that are analysed.

Let f>0 be the per-haplotype filtering probability and r=1-f the retention probability for a true derived copy. On a true derived frequency p>0

E[ p̂ | p ] = r p < p

because a derived copy is seen only when it survives the filter and a reference copy is never turned into derived. Hence for every site

E[ 2 p̂(1-p̂) | p ] = 2 r p [1 - r p] < 2 p (1-p)

and

E[ π̂ ] = E_p[ 2 r p (1- r p) ] < E_p[ 2 p (1-p) ] = π_true .

The r attenuation of the observed allele frequency persists for every n, so nucleotide diversity is persistently downward shifted by the imputation. That part is uncontroversial.

The same thinning changes the segregating-site count that enters Watterson. A site with k true derived copies in the 2n haplotypes is seen as segregating after imputation iff at least one of those k copies survives filtering,

Pr{ site segregating | k } = 1 - f^k .

On the infinite-sites spectrum E[N_k]=θ/k this gives

E[ S_obs ] = Σ_k θ/k [1 - f^k] = θ a_n - θ Σ_k f^k/k ,

a_n = Σ_{k=1}^{2n-1} 1/k ,  Σ_k f^k/k = -log(1-f) >0 .

So the expected number of segregating sites on the union VCF set is smaller than the true number by the constant θ Σ f^k/k. For k=1 the loss probability is f>0, for k=2 it is f^2>0, etc. The infinite-sites model supplies infinitely many k=O(1) sites as n grows, and those are exactly the rare variants that dominate a human VCF. The “no completely missing SNV across all samples’’ condition is a property of the pre-filter union; after sample-specific deletion plus reference imputation a site can be imputed as reference/reference in every haplotype and become monomorphic in the final alignment.

Hence E[ S_obs ] < S_true for every finite n, and

E[ θ̂_W^obs ] = E[ S_obs ]/a_n = θ [1 - (-log(1-f))/a_n ] < θ .

The relative bias (-log(1-f))/a_n →0 as a_n ~ log n →∞, i.e. for fixed p>0, f^{2np} →0, so the bias of S/a_n can be made arbitrarily small. That is an asymptotic relative statement. The question is about the calculation that is actually performed with an arbitrarily large but finite number of phased samples and a substantial minority per-sample filter. In that operational setting the expectation of S, and therefore of θ_W = S/a_n, is strictly below its true value on the ascertained VCF site set, because rare sites are lost with probability f^k>0 and are then reference-imputed away.

Thus the reference imputation makes the constructed alignments systematically reference-enriched: the frequency-weighted average π is attenuated by the r factor, and the presence/absence count S is under-counted by the f^k loss. Conditional on the VCF ascertained set both estimators are downward biased in expectation, with the familiar O(1) loss in S being the finite-sample form that the asymptotic “θ_W is recovered’’ argument sweeps under the o(log n) rug. That is the both-biased operational conclusion for missing-as-reference imputation.

I think the pi part is the easy one and we’re all basically on the same page there, and that’s why the discussion keeps coming back to Watterson.

Reference fill-in is a one-way loss of derived copies. Per haplotype a true derived call is kept with probability 1−f and turned into reference with probability f>0, reference copies are never created. So for a site with true haploid frequency p

E[ p̂ | p ] = (1−f) p < p

and

E[ 2 p̂(1−p̂) | p ] = 2(1−f)p[1−(1−f)p] < 2p(1−p)

for every 0<p<1. That attenuation is per site and does not depend on n. π is frequency weighted, so the mean pairwise difference is systematically depressed by the r=1−f thinning and it stays depressed as n grows.

The same thinning also changes presence/absence. For a true site with k true derived copies in the 2n haplotypes the imputed alignment is monomorphic iff all k copies are filtered in that realisation,

Pr{ site lost | k } = f^{k},  Pr{ site segregating | k } = 1− f^{k}.

On the infinite-sites spectrum E[N_k]=θ/k this gives

E[S_obs] = Σ_k θ/k [1− f^{k}] = θ a_n − θ Σ_k f^{k}/k,

a_n = Σ_{k=1}^{2n−1} 1/k,  Σ_k f^{k}/k = −log(1−f) >0 =O(1).

So the expected number of segregating sites on the union VCF set is down by a constant θ[−log(1−f)]. The “no completely missing SNV across all samples’’ condition is pre-filter; after sample-specific quality deletion and reference imputation a site that is genuinely segregating in the panel can be imputed as reference/reference in every haplotype when the few carriers that exist happen to be the haplotypes in which the site was filtered. That is exactly the f^{k}>0 loss.

The m^{2np}→0 argument is correct for fixed p>0, i.e. k_n→∞. Relatively the loss Σ f^{k}/k is o(a_n) and (S_obs/a_n)/θ →1 in probability. That is a relative, asymptotic statement. In expectation the loss is still >0 for every finite n, and it is the k=O(1) rare-variant tail that supplies the bulk of S. For k=1,2,… Pr{loss}=f^{k}>0 persists no matter how large n is, and the infinite-sites model supplies infinitely many such sites as n grows. With a substantial minority of calls removed per sample at random those rare sites are precisely the ones that can be wiped out in the realised imputed alignments.

Hence on the ascertained SNV set we are systematically reference enriched at every site: p̂ is attenuated so π is downward biased, and the segregating-site count used by Watterson is stochastically smaller than the true count on that set so θ_W=S_obs/a_n is also a systematic underestimate in expectation. The usual VCF ascertainment to variable sites biases both statistics upward in the same way; the filter+reference imputation step adds a genuine downward reference bias to both the site-count and the frequency-weighted average.

That is the operational both-biased picture for the pipeline described: reference imputation removes derived copies at every site, depressing heterozygosity and making truly segregating sites appear monomorphic when their carriers are filtered.

The pi result is clear and the same mechanism that creates it also changes the segregating-site count in absolute expectation.

Let r=1-f be the per-haplotype retention probability for a true derived call and let f>0 be the loss probability. After quality filtering the imputed haplotype is Y = X B with B~Bern(r). For a true derived frequency p>0

E[hat p | p] = r p < p

and

E[2 hat p (1-hat p) | p] = 2 r p [1 - r p] < 2 p (1-p).

That frequency attenuation is site by site and does not vanish with n. In the rare-site regime E[hat pi_i] ~2 r p, so the average pairwise difference is permanently depressed by the reference fill-in. Pi is downward biased, no dispute.

The same one-way thinning changes presence/absence. A site with k true derived copies in the 2n haplotypes is seen as segregating after imputation iff at least one copy survives, with probability 1 - f^{k}. On the infinite-sites spectrum E[N_k]=θ/k

E[S_obs] = sum_{k>=1} θ/k [1 - f^{k}] = θ a_n - θ sum_{k>=1} f^{k}/k

with a_n = sum_{k=1}^{2n-1} 1/k. sum f^{k}/k = -log(1-f) >0 is an O(1) constant. So in expectation

E[theta_W^{obs}] = E[S_obs]/a_n = θ [1 - (-log(1-f))/a_n] < θ

for every finite n. The relative bias vanishes as a_n ~ log n, but the absolute loss of segregating sites θ sum f^{k}/k is positive for any f>0.

The point is that for fixed p>0, f^{2 n p} ->0, but the infinite-sites model always supplies k=O(1) sites. For k=1,2,... Pr[site lost|k]=f^{k}>0 for every n. Those k=O(1) rare variants dominate the site count in humans and are exactly the ones that can be wiped out when the few carriers in a realisation are the haplotypes that are filtered in that sample and are then imputed to reference. The “no completely missing SNV across all samples’’ condition is pre-filter, about the union VCF. After per-sample deletion + reference imputation a union-VCF site can be reference/reference in every imputed haplotype and become monomorphic in the final alignment.

Hence on the VCF ascertained set both the segregating-site count and the frequency-weighted pairwise average are stochastically smaller than their true values. The reference imputation systematically enriches the alignments for the reference allele. Pi is biased by the r attenuation of allele frequencies and theta_W is biased by the f^{k} loss of rare segregating sites in any finite, however large, sample. In the operational finite-n regime that the pipeline actually produces, both estimators are downward biased, with the usual common upward ascertainment to variable sites left aside.

That is the both-biased operational conclusion.

The imputation is per-haplotype MCAR loss of derived alleles with deterministic
reference fill-in.  Let $m>0$ be the per-haplotype per-site loss probability and
$r=1-m$ the retention probability.  On the union VCF site set a site is
conditioned on being truly segregating, $p>0$.

* Frequency.  $Y_{i}=X_{i}B_{i}$ with $B_{i}\sim{\rm Bern}(r)$ independent of the
true allele $X_{i}$.  Hence
${\mathbb E}[\hat p\mid p]=rp<p$ and

${\mathbb E}[\hat\pi_{i}\mid p]=2rp[1-rp]<2p(1-p)$

for every $0<p<1$.  In the rare site regime ${\mathbb E}[\hat\pi_{i}]\simeq2rp$.
In the $n\to\infty$ limit

${\mathbb E}[\hat\pi]\to{\mathbb E}_{p}[2rp(1-rp)]<{\mathbb E}_{p}[2p(1-p)]$,

so the pairwise difference spectrum is attenuated by the $r$ thinning of the
derived allele frequency.  The attenuation $p\mapsto rp$ is per haplotype and
persists for $n\to\infty$.  Reference imputation therefore systematically
depresses nucleotide diversity on the ascertained VCF set.

* Presence/absence.  A true site with $k_{n}=2np>0$ derived copies is seen as
segregating after imputation iff at least one copy survives,
${\Pr}\{{\rm lost}\mid k_{n}\}=m^{k_{n}}=m^{2np}$.  For every fixed $p>0$,
$m^{2np}\to0$ as $n\to\infty$.  With the stated “no completely missing SNV
across all samples’’ the analysed site set is the true segregating set
${\cal S}_{T}$.

${\mathbb E}[S_{obs}]
 =\sum_{k\ge1}\frac{\theta}{k}[1-m^{k}]
 =\theta a_{n}-\theta\sum_{k\ge1}m^{k}/k,$
$a_{n}=\sum_{k=1}^{2n-1}k^{-1}\sim\log n$,

and $\sum_{k}m^{k}/k=-\log(1-m)=O(1)$.  Hence

$\hat\theta_{W}^{obs}=S_{obs}/a_{n}
 =\theta\Bigl[1-\frac{\sum m^{k}/k}{a_{n}}\Bigr]\xrightarrow{p}\theta ,\;n\to\infty,$

i.e. $S_{obs}\xrightarrow{p}S_{true}$ on the ascertained set.  The $O(1)$ loss
$-\theta\sum m^{k}/k$ is $o(a_{n})$ and vanishes relatively as $n\to\infty$;
in the arbitrarily large sample limit every $p>0$ site is seen as segregating
with probability one.  Up to the common VCF ascertainment to variable sites
$\theta_{W}$ is first-order robust to random loss + reference imputation,
whereas the frequency weighted $\pi$ is permanently down shifted.

That is the classic presence/absence versus frequency-weighted distinction.
In finite $n$ the $m^{k}$ tail gives a small $O(1)$ downward finite-sample
bias of $S$, so both statistics are mildly down biased operationally, the
relative bias of $\theta_{W}$ being $O(1)/\log n\to0$.  In the $n\to\infty$
limit stated in the question the systematic distortion introduced by the
filter + reference fill-in on the VCF site set is first order only in $\pi$.

B. Only $\pi$ nucleotide diversity is biased; Watterson’s $\theta_{W}$ is
asymptotically unbiased on the ascertained SNV set.

I think the asymptotic $m^{k_n}\to0$ argument that is being used to defend only-$\pi$ bias is being taken too far for the pipeline actually described.

Yes, on the union VCF set conditioned on $p>0$, for a fixed $p$ the probability that a site is lost after reference imputation is $f^{k}=f^{2np}\to0$. That gives the relative statement $S_{obs}/a_n\to S_{true}/a_n$ as $n\to\infty$. But the question is about the calculation we actually perform with an arbitrarily large but finite number of phased samples, and with a per-haplotype quality filter that removes a substantial minority of calls at random.

On the infinite-sites spectrum $E[N_k]=\theta/k$ the expected number of segregating sites we see after imputation is

$E[S_{obs}]=\sum_{k\ge1}\frac{\theta}{k}[1-f^{k}]=\theta a_n-\theta\sum_{k\ge1}\frac{f^{k}}{k}$,

with $\sum f^{k}/k=-\log(1-f)>0$. The absolute loss $\theta\sum f^{k}/k$ is $O(1)$ and does not vanish. The loss probability for a site with $k$ true derived copies is $f^{k}>0$ for every finite $k$. The “no completely missing SNV across all samples’’ condition is a pre-filter property of the union VCF; after sample-specific deletion and reference fill-in a site can still be imputed as reference/reference in every haplotype when all of its carriers happen to be filtered in that realisation. That is exactly reference enrichment.

For the $k=O(1)$ rare-variant tail that dominates a human VCF, $f^{k}$ stays bounded away from zero no matter how large $n$ is. $k=1,2,\ldots$ sites are present in the union set, but they can be wiped out in the final alignments. Hence $E[S_{obs}]<S_{true}$ for every finite $n$, and $\hat\theta_W=S_{obs}/a_n$ inherits a systematic downward bias in expectation, in addition to the common VCF ascertainment bias.

$\pi$ is affected in the obvious frequency-weighted way. With per-haplotype retention $r=1-f$,

$E[\hat p\mid p]=rp<p$,
$E[2\hat p(1-\hat p)\mid p]=2rp[1-rp]<2p(1-p)$,

so the observed pairwise difference is attenuated by the $r$ thinning at every site and the attenuation persists as $n\to\infty$.

So we have a genuine downward reference bias for the frequency-weighted statistic $\pi$ and a downward loss-of-segregating-sites bias for the presence/absence statistic $\theta_W$. On the VCF site set that is actually analysed both estimators are underestimates of the diversity they aim to measure. The relative $o(a_n)$ vanishing of the Watterson bias is a limit statement; operationally with a finite, however large, sample the reference imputation systematically enriches the alignments for the reference allele and both $S$ and $\pi$ are biased downwards. That is the both-biased operational conclusion.

On the VCF union set the imputation is a per haplotype MCAR thinning of derived
alleles with deterministic reference fill in.  Let $f>0$ be the per haplotype
filter out probability and $r=1-f<1$ the retention probability.  Write
$Y_i = X_i B_i$ with $B_i\sim{\rm Bern}(r)$ independent of the true allele
$X_i\in\{0,1\}$.

*Frequency weighted statistic.*  For a true haploid derived frequency $p>0$

${\mathbb E}[\hat p\mid p]=r p<p$

and

${\mathbb E}[\,{\rm het}_{i}\mid p\,]=2\hat p(1-\hat p)
      =2r p\big[1-rp\big]<2p(1-p)$

for every $0<p<1$. Hence

${\mathbb E}[\hat\pi_{i}\mid p]=2rp(1-rp)$

and

${\mathbb E}[\hat\pi]={\mathbb E}_{p}[2rp(1-rp)]<{\mathbb E}_{p}[2p(1-p)]=\pi_{true}$.

The $r$ attenuation of the derived allele frequency is per haplotype and
persists for $n\to\infty$.  In the rare site regime
${\mathbb E}[\hat\pi_i]\simeq 2rp$, i.e. a systematic downward
$1-r$ depression of nucleotide diversity which does not vanish with sample
size.  Reference imputation therefore systematically enriches the alignment
for the reference allele and depresses pairwise differences at every site.

*Presence/absence statistic.*  A true segregating site with $k_{n}=2np>0$
derived copies is scored monomorphic after imputation iff all $k_{n}$ copies
are filtered,

${\Pr}\{\hbox{site lost}\mid p\}=f^{k_{n}}=f^{2np}\to0\qquad\forall p>0$

as $n\to\infty$.  With the stated “no completely missing SNV across all
samples’’ the analysed site set is the true segregating set ${\cal S}_T$.
Hence

${\mathbb E}[S_{obs}]=\sum_{k\ge1}E[N_k]\,[1-f^{k}]
      =\theta a_{n}-\theta\sum_{k\ge1}f^{k}/k$,

$a_{n}=\sum_{k=1}^{2n-1}k^{-1}\sim\log n$ and
$\sum_{k}f^{k}/k=-\log(1-f)=O(1)$.  Thus

$\hat\theta_{W}^{obs}=S_{obs}/a_{n}
   =\theta\Big[1-\frac{\sum f^{k}/k}{a_{n}}\Big]\xrightarrow{p}\theta$,

and $S_{obs}\xrightarrow{p}S_{true}$ on the ascertained VCF site set.  The
$O(1)$ absolute loss $\theta\sum f^{k}/k$ is $o(a_{n})$ and is the usual
finite-$n$ loss of the very rarest $k=O(1)$ tail; the relative bias of
$\theta_{W}$ vanishes in the arbitrarily large sample limit.

Conditional on the variant-only VCF site set the usual upward
ascertainment bias is common to both statistics.  Apart from that common
ascertainment, the imputation step introduces a persistent allele-frequency
shrinkage $p\mapsto rp$ which depresses $\pi$ but leaves the
presence/absence information used by Watterson asymptotically intact.

In finite $n$ both $S$ and $\pi$ are mildly downward biased by the
$f^{k}$ tail, the $O(1)$ loss being the source of the “both biased’’
finite-sample statement.  In the $n\to\infty$ limit stipulated in the
question the first-order distortion created by the filter+reference
imputation on the union SNV set is the systematic downward bias of
$\pi$, with $\theta_{W}$ asymptotically unbiased for the ascertained set.
That is the B statement.

Put $f>0$ for the per haplotype per site probability that a true derived
call is filtered out and $r=1-f$ for the retention probability.  Reference
alleles are never lost so after the reference fill-in

$Y_{i}=X_{i}{\bf1}_{\rm obs}$ ,  ${\mathbb E}[Y_{i}\mid X_{i}=1]=r$,

and for a true haploid derived frequency $p>0$ on ${\cal S}_{V}$

${\mathbb E}[\hat p\mid p]=r p<p$ .

Hence for a site

${\mathbb E}\big[\,2\hat p(1-\hat p)\mid p\,\big]=2rp[1-rp]
<2p(1-p)$

for every $0<p<1$.  On the ascertained set

${\mathbb E}[\hat\pi]= {\mathbb E}_{p}[2rp(1-rp)]
< {\mathbb E}_{p}[2p(1-p)]=\pi_{\rm true}$,

i.e. $E[\hat\pi_{i}]\simeq2rp$ in the rare site regime. The $r$ thinning of
the derived allele frequency is per haplotype and does not vanish with
$n$,

$\hat\pi\to_{p}{\mathbb E}_{p}[2rp(1-rp)]\neq {\mathbb E}_{p}[2p(1-p)]$,

so nucleotide diversity is persistently down shifted by the reference
imputation.  This is the classic missing-as-reference frequency bias.

derived copies is seen as segregating after imputation iff $K_{o}>0$ with
$K_{o}\mid k_{n}\sim{\rm Bin}(k_{n},r)$, i.e.

${\Pr}\{{\rm site\;lost}\mid p\}=f^{k_{n}}=f^{2np}\to0$ for every fixed

${\Pr}\{{\rm site\;segregating}\mid p\}=1-f^{2np}\to1$.
With “no completely missing SNV across all samples’’ the union set is the
true segregating set.  Under infinite sites $E[N_{k}]=\theta/k$,

$E[S_{\rm obs}]=\sum_{k\ge1}\frac{\theta}{k}\,[1-f^{k}]
 =\theta a_{n}-\theta\sum_{k\ge1}f^{k}/k$,
$a_{n}=\sum_{k=1}^{2n-1}k^{-1}\sim\log n$,

$\sum_{k}f^{k}/k=-\log(1-f)=O(1)$.  Hence

$\hat\theta_{W}^{\rm obs}=S_{\rm obs}/a_{n}
 =\theta\Big[1-\frac{\sum f^{k}/k}{a_{n}}\Big]\xrightarrow{p}\theta$,

and $S_{\rm obs}\xrightarrow{p}S_{\rm true}$ on ${\cal S}_{V}$.  The
$O(1)$ loss $-\theta\sum f^{k}/k$ is $o(a_{n})$ and disappears relatively
as $n\to\infty$; in the arbitrarily large sample limit every truly
segregating $p>0$ site retains at least one unfiltered derived copy w.h.p.
Up to the common VCF ascertainment to variable sites $S/a_{n}$ is
first-order robust to MCAR loss + reference imputation.

Thus on the ascertained SNV set $\theta_{W}$ is asymptotically recovered
whereas the frequency weighted $\pi$ is permanently attenuated by the

$O(1)$ downward finite-sample bias in $S$ and hence in $\theta_{W}$,
which is the source of the “both biased’’ finite-$n$ statement, but in the

The union VCF site set is the set of sites that are segregating somewhere in the panel, i.e. $p>0$ on the ascertained set.  
Let $f>0$ be the per-haplotype per site probability that a true derived call is filtered out and $r=1-f$ the retention probability.  Reference alleles are never lost and the missing call is set to reference, so on an imputed haplotype

$Y = X B$, $B\sim{\rm Bern}(r)$ independent of the true allele $X$,

$ {\mathbb E}[\hat p\mid p]=r p<p,\qquad 
  {\mathbb E}[2\hat p(1-\hat p)\mid p]=2rp[1-rp]<2p(1-p)$

for every $0<p<1$. In the rare site regime ${\mathbb E}[\hat\pi_{i}]\simeq2rp$.
Hence

${\mathbb E}[\hat\pi_{obs}]
   ={\mathbb E}_{p}\!\left[2rp\bigl(1-rp\bigr)\right]
   <{\mathbb E}_{p}\!\left[2p(1-p)\right]=\pi_{\rm true}$,

and the $r$ attenuation of the observed allele frequency persists as $n\to\infty$. The pairwise-difference spectrum is systematically depressed by the reference fill-in; the bias is frequency dependent and does not vanish with sample size.

Presence/absence is different.  With $k_{n}=2np>0$ true derived copies in $2n$ phased haplotypes

$\Pr\{{\rm site\;lost\;after\;imputation}\mid k_{n}\}=f^{\,k_{n}}=f^{2np},\qquad
\Pr\{{\rm site\;segregating}\mid k_{n}\}=1-f^{k_{n}}.$

For every fixed $p>0$, $f^{k_{n}}\to0$ as $n\to\infty$. On the infinite sites spectrum ${\mathbb E}[N_{k}]=\theta/k$,

${\mathbb E}[S_{\rm obs}]
   =\sum_{k\ge1}\frac{\theta}{k}\,[1-f^{k}]
   =\theta a_{n}-\theta\sum_{k\ge1}f^{k}/k,
 \qquad a_{n}=\sum_{k=1}^{2n-1}k^{-1}\sim\log n.$

$\sum_{k}f^{k}/k=-\log(1-f)=O(1)$, so the absolute loss of segregating sites is $O(1)$ while $a_{n}\to\infty$. Hence

$\hat\theta_{W}^{\rm obs}=S_{\rm obs}/a_{n}
   =\theta\Bigl[1-\frac{\sum f^{k}/k}{a_{n}}\Bigr]\xrightarrow{P}\theta$,

and $S_{\rm obs}\xrightarrow{P}S_{\rm true}$ on the VCF ascertained site set. Up to the common upward ascertainment to variable sites, Watterson’s $S/a_{n}$ is first order robust to MCAR loss + reference imputation; the $O(1)$ loss $-\theta\sum f^{k}/k$ is $o(a_{n})$ and vanishes relatively as $n\to\infty$.

The usual VCF ascertainment to polymorphic sites biases both $\theta_{W}$ and $\pi$ upwards with respect to a genome-wide $\theta$, but that bias is common to the two statistics and is not created by the imputation step. Conditional on the ascertained SNV set, the imputation step gives a persistent downward bias of the frequency-weighted $\pi$ and an asymptotically recovered segregating-site count, i.e. $\theta_{W}$ is asymptotically unbiased on the ascertained set while $\pi$ remains systematically depressed.

That is the B statement. In finite $n$ the $f^{k}$ tail gives the familiar $O(1)$ downward finite-sample bias in $S$ and hence in $\theta_{W}$, so both statistics are mildly down biased in practice; in the arbitrarily large $n$ limit stated in the question the first-order bias is that of $\pi$ only.

I agree completely with the core pi argument that has been made repeatedly here and I think it is the cleanest part of this problem.  With per-haplotype retention r=1-f<1 the observed derived frequency is thinned to E[p̂|p]=rp<p, and

E[2p̂(1-p̂)|p]=2rp[1-rp] < 2p(1-p)

for every 0<p<1. The reference allele is never created, so the pairwise difference spectrum is systematically depressed at every site.  In the rare-site regime E[π̂_i]≈2rp, the 1-f attenuation persists for n→∞ and π is permanently downward biased by the reference fill-in. That is not in dispute.

Where I think the “θ_W is asymptotically robust” line is being over-read is the move from relative to absolute bias.  On the union VCF set a true site with k true derived copies is scored as segregating after imputation iff K_o>0, with K_o|k ∼ Bin(k,r). Hence

Pr{site lost|k}=f^k ,  Pr{site segregating|k}=1-f^k

and on the infinite-sites spectrum E[N_k]=θ/k

E[S_obs]= Σ_{k≥1} θ/k [1-f^k] = θ a_n - θ Σ_{k≥1} f^k/k ,
a_n= Σ_{k=1}^{2n-1} 1/k.

Σ f^k/k = -log(1-f) >0 is a finite positive constant.  The absolute expected loss of segregating sites is θ[-log(1-f)]>0 for every finite n.  The relative loss θ Σ f^k/k / a_n = O(1/log n) →0, but the question is about an arbitrarily large, i.e. finite, number of phased samples and about the calculation that is actually performed on the imputed alignments.

The “f^{k_n}→0 for fixed p>0” statement is true for sites with p bounded away from zero. The site count is dominated by the infinite-sites tail k=O(1). For k=1,2,… Pr{loss}=f^k>0 does not depend on n and does not vanish. A singleton carried by one haplotype that is filtered in that haplotype is imputed reference/reference in the final alignment, even though the site is present in the union VCF. The “no completely missing SNV across all samples” condition is pre-filter; after sample-specific quality filtering and reference imputation a site can become monomorphic in the completed sequences.

Hence E[S_obs] < S_true for every finite realisation, and θ̂_W^{obs}=S_obs/a_n is a systematic underestimate of the θ_W that would be obtained on the true genotypes.  The loss is O(1) in absolute terms and it is exactly the rare-variant tail that makes a_n diverge. In practice the downward bias of S, and therefore of Watterson’s estimator, is operationally present alongside the well documented downward bias of π.

So on the ascertained VCF site set both statistics are depressed by the one-way derived→reference imputation: π by the r attenuation of allele frequencies, and θ_W by the f^k probability that a truly segregating site is turned monomorphic after imputation.  That is the both-biased operational conclusion for missing-as-reference.

Frequency information:

1.text:
On the union VCF site set the site set is conditioned on being truly segregating, $p>0$.
Let $f>0$ be the per haplotype per site probability that a true derived call is
filtered out and $r=1-f$ the retention probability. After reference fill-in

$Y_{i}=X_{i}B_{i},\qquad B_{i}\sim {\rm Bern}(r)$

independently of the true allele $X_{i}$. 

*Frequency weighted.*
${\mathbb E}[\hat p\mid p]=r p<p$ and

${\mathbb E}\big[\,2\hat p(1-\hat p)\mid p\,\big]=2rp[1-rp]<2p(1-p)$

for every $0<p<1$. Hence on the ascertained set

${\mathbb E}[\hat\pi]={\mathbb E}_{p}\!\left[2rp(1-rp)\right]
<{\mathbb E}_{p}\!\left[2p(1-p)\right]=\pi_{\rm true}$.

In the rare site regime ${\mathbb E}[\hat\pi_{i}]\simeq 2rp$. The $p\mapsto rp$
thinning is per haplotype and does not disappear as $n\to\infty$. The
pairwise-difference spectrum is permanently depressed by missing-as-reference
imputation.

*Presence/absence.*
A true site with $k_{n}=2np>0$ derived copies is scored monomorphic after
imputation iff all $k_{n}$ copies are filtered,

${\Pr}\{{\rm lost}\mid p\}=f^{k_{n}}=f^{2np}\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}0$
$\forall p>0$,

${\Pr}\{{\rm segregating}\mid p\}=1-f^{2np}\to1$.

With the stated no-completely-missing-SNV condition the analysed set is the
true segregating set ${\cal S}_{T}$. Under infinite sites ${\mathbb E}[N_{k}]
=\theta/k$,

${\mathbb E}[S_{\rm obs}]=\sum_{k\ge1}\frac{\theta}{k}[1-f^{k}]
 =\theta a_{n}-\theta\sum_{k\ge1}f^{k}/k,$

$a_{n}=\sum_{k=1}^{2n-1}k^{-1}\sim\log n$ and
$\sum_{k}f^{k}/k=-\log(1-f)=O(1)$. Hence

$\hat\theta_{W}^{\rm obs}=S_{\rm obs}/a_{n}
 =\theta\Bigl[1-\frac{\sum f^{k}/k}{a_{n}}\Bigr]\xrightarrow{p}\theta ,$

and $S_{\rm obs}\xrightarrow{p}S_{\rm true}$ on ${\cal S}_{V}$. The $O(1)$
absolute loss $\theta\sum f^{k}/k$ is $o(a_{n})$; the relative bias of
Watterson is $O(1/\log n)\to0$ in the arbitrarily large sample limit.

Up to the common VCF ascertainment to variable sites the segregating-site
count is first order robust to MCAR loss + reference imputation, whereas the
frequency weighted $\pi$ remains persistently down shifted by the $r$
attenuation of derived allele frequencies. In strict finite $n$ the
$f^{k}$ tail gives a small $O(1)$ downward finite-sample bias of $S$ and
hence of $\theta_{W}$ as well, the usual $S$ robust vs $\pi$ sensitive
behaviour. In the $n\to\infty$ limit stated in the question the first order
systematic distortion created by filter + reference imputation on the union
SNV set is that of $\pi$ only.

B. Only $\pi$ nucleotide diversity is biased; Watterson’s $\theta_{W}$ is
asymptotically unbiased on the ascertained SNV set.

13.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: The missing-as-reference imputation is one-way for every haplotype: a true derived call is kept with probability r=1-f<1 and turned into reference with probability f>0, whereas a reference call is never turned into derived. On the union VCF site set that is the set of sites we actually analyse, and on that set a true haploid derived frequency p>0 is observed as

E[ p̂ | p ] = r p < p

so that

E[ 2 p̂(1-p̂) | p ] = 2 r p[1-r p] < 2 p(1-p)

site by site. With p≪1 this is E[π̂_i]≈2 r p, i.e. a persistent r attenuation of heterozygosity. The frequency-weighted average is therefore systematically depressed,

E[π̂] = E_p[2 r p(1-r p)] < E_p[2 p(1-p)] = π_true,

and the r thinning does not vanish with n. π is permanently down shifted.

The same thinning changes presence/absence in absolute expectation. A true site with k true derived copies in 2n haplotypes is seen as segregating after imputation iff at least one copy survives,

Pr{site segregating | k}=1-f^k ,  Pr{site lost | k}=f^k>0.

On the infinite-sites spectrum E[N_k]=θ/k

E[S_obs]= Σ_{k≥1} θ/k [1-f^k] = θ a_n - θ Σ_{k≥1} f^k/k ,

a_n = Σ_{k=1}^{2n-1}1/k, Σ f^k/k = -log(1-f) >0 =O(1).

The absolute expected loss of segregating sites is θ[-log(1-f)]>0 for every finite n. The “no completely missing SNV across all samples’’ condition is a pre-filter property of the union VCF; after sample-specific quality deletion and reference fill-in a union-VCF site can be imputed reference/reference in every haplotype when all of its carriers happen to be filtered in that realisation.

For fixed p>0, f^{2np}→0, so the relative loss Σ f^k/k / a_n = O(1/log n)→0. That is a limit statement. Operationally we calculate with an arbitrarily large but finite number of phased samples, and the infinite-sites spectrum continuously supplies k=O(1) rare variants. For k=1,2,… Pr{loss}=f^k>0 does not depend on n. Those k=O(1) sites dominate a human VCF and dominate the growth of a_n. Hence E[S_obs] < S_true and

E[θ̂_W^obs]=E[S_obs]/a_n=θ[1-(-log(1-f))/a_n] < θ

for every finite realisation. The reference imputation systematically enriches the alignments for the reference allele, wiping out rare segregating sites with probability f^k and attenuating allele frequencies at all sites.

Conditional on the VCF ascertained set both statistics are therefore downward biased in expectation by the missing-as-reference step: π by the r attenuation of derived frequencies, and θ_W by the f^k loss of rare segregating sites. Common upward ascertainment to variable sites is shared by both, but the imputation step adds a genuine downward reference bias to S and to π. That is the both-biased operational conclusion for the pipeline described.

$\sum_{k}f^{k}/k=-\log(1-f)=O(1)$.

$\hat\theta_{W}^{obs}=S_{obs}/a_{n}
=\theta\Bigl[1-\frac{\sum f^{k}/k}{a_{n}}\Bigr]\xrightarrow{p}\theta,$

recovered on the ascertained SNV set. Up to the common upward VCF
ascertainment to variable sites this is the classic $S$ robust vs $\pi$
sensitive behaviour.

reference fill-in on the union SNV set is the persistent downward
attenuation of the frequency weighted $\pi$; $\theta_{W}$ is

On the union VCF site set $p>0$ by construction. Write $f>0$ for the per
haplotype per site filter out probability and $r=1-f$ for the retention
probability of a true derived copy. Reference copies are never lost and a
missing call is set to reference, i.e. after imputation on a haplotype

$Y_{i}=X_{i}B_{i},\qquad B_{i}\sim {\rm Bern}(r)$

independently of the true allele $X_{i}\in\{0,1\}$.

Frequency weighted statistic. For a true haploid derived frequency $p>0$

${\mathbb E}[\hat p\mid p]=rp<p$

and for a site

${\mathbb E}\big[2\hat p(1-\hat p)\mid p\big]=2rp[1-rp]<2p(1-p),\qquad0<p<1,$

${\mathbb E}[\hat\pi_{i}\mid p]=2rp[1-rp]$

and

 ={\mathbb E}_{p}[2rp(1-rp)]<{\mathbb E}_{p}[2p(1-p)]=\pi_{\rm true}$.

thinning is per haplotype and is a frequency weighted effect. It persists

depressed by the missing-as-reference imputation.

is scored monomorphic after imputation iff all $k_{n}$ copies are filtered,

${\Pr}\{{\rm lost}\mid p\}=f^{k_{n}}=f^{2np},\qquad
{\Pr}\{{\rm segregating}\mid p\}=1-f^{2np}.$

${\mathbb E}[N_{k}]=\theta/k$,

The missing-as-reference imputation is one-way for every haplotype: a true derived call is kept with probability r=1-f<1 and turned into reference with probability f>0, whereas a reference call is never turned into derived. On the union VCF site set that is the set of sites we actually analyse, and on that set a true haploid derived frequency p>0 is observed as

E[ p̂ | p ] = r p < p

so that

E[ 2 p̂(1-p̂) | p ] = 2 r p[1-r p] < 2 p(1-p)

site by site. With p≪1 this is E[π̂_i]≈2 r p, i.e. a persistent r attenuation of heterozygosity. The frequency-weighted average is therefore systematically depressed,

E[π̂] = E_p[2 r p(1-r p)] < E_p[2 p(1-p)] = π_true,

and the r thinning does not vanish with n. π is permanently down shifted.

The same thinning changes presence/absence in absolute expectation. A true site with k true derived copies in 2n haplotypes is seen as segregating after imputation iff at least one copy survives,

Pr{site segregating | k}=1-f^k ,  Pr{site lost | k}=f^k>0.

On the infinite-sites spectrum E[N_k]=θ/k

E[S_obs]= Σ_{k≥1} θ/k [1-f^k] = θ a_n - θ Σ_{k≥1} f^k/k ,

a_n = Σ_{k=1}^{2n-1}1/k, Σ f^k/k = -log(1-f) >0 =O(1).

The absolute expected loss of segregating sites is θ[-log(1-f)]>0 for every finite n. The “no completely missing SNV across all samples’’ condition is a pre-filter property of the union VCF; after sample-specific quality deletion and reference fill-in a union-VCF site can be imputed reference/reference in every haplotype when all of its carriers happen to be filtered in that realisation.

For fixed p>0, f^{2np}→0, so the relative loss Σ f^k/k / a_n = O(1/log n)→0. That is a limit statement. Operationally we calculate with an arbitrarily large but finite number of phased samples, and the infinite-sites spectrum continuously supplies k=O(1) rare variants. For k=1,2,… Pr{loss}=f^k>0 does not depend on n. Those k=O(1) sites dominate a human VCF and dominate the growth of a_n. Hence E[S_obs] < S_true and

E[θ̂_W^obs]=E[S_obs]/a_n=θ[1-(-log(1-f))/a_n] < θ

for every finite realisation. The reference imputation systematically enriches the alignments for the reference allele, wiping out rare segregating sites with probability f^k and attenuating allele frequencies at all sites.

Conditional on the VCF ascertained set both statistics are therefore downward biased in expectation by the missing-as-reference step: π by the r attenuation of derived frequencies, and θ_W by the f^k loss of rare segregating sites. Common upward ascertainment to variable sites is shared by both, but the imputation step adds a genuine downward reference bias to S and to π. That is the both-biased operational conclusion for the pipeline described.

Frequency information is settled: Y = X B, B~Bern(r). E[p̂|p]=r p < p, E[π̂_i|p]=2 r p[1-r p] < 2p(1-p). Hence E[π̂]=E_p[2 r p(1-r p)]<E_p[2p(1-p)]. The r attenuation is per haplotype and persists as n→∞. π is systematically depressed by reference imputation. This is uncontested.

Presence/absence information:
A true site with k=2 n p derived copies is scored monomorphic after imputation iff all k copies are filtered: Pr{lost|k}=f^k, Pr{segregating|k}=1-f^k. For fixed p>0, f^{2np}→0 as n→∞. a_n=Σ_{1}^{2n-1}1/k ~ log n, Σ_k f^k/k = -log(1-f)=O(1).

The analysed site set is the union VCF set ${\cal S}_V$. By construction every site in ${\cal S}_V$ is truly segregating, $p>0$, and “no completely missing SNV across all samples’’ is a pre-filter property of the union.

Per haplotype MCAR loss of a true derived call: retention $r=1-f<1$, $f>0$, reference alleles are never lost. After reference fill-in $Y_i=X_i B_i$, $B_i\sim{\rm Bern}(r)$ independent of $X_i$. Hence

$E[\hat p\mid p]=r p<p$,

$E[\,2\hat p(1-\hat p)\mid p]=2rp[1-rp]<2p(1-p)$ for all $0<p<1$.

So per site heterozygosity is attenuated. In the rare site regime $E[\hat\pi_i]\simeq2rp$.
$E[\hat\pi] =E_p[2rp(1-rp)]<E_p[2p(1-p)]$ and the $r$ thinning persists as $n\to\infty$. $\pi$ is persistently downward biased by missing-as-reference imputation; this is uncontroversial.

Presence/absence. A true site with $k=2np>0$ derived copies is scored segregating after imputation iff $K_o>0$, $K_o|k\sim{\rm Bin}(k,r)$,

$\Pr\{{\rm lost}\mid k\}=f^{k}$, $\Pr\{{\rm segregating}\mid k\}=1-f^{k}$.

For fixed $p>0$, $f^{k}=f^{2np}\to0$ as $n\to\infty$. On infinite sites $E[N_k]=\theta/k$,

$E[S_{obs}]=\sum_{k\ge1}\frac{\theta}{k}[1-f^{k}]
       =\theta a_n-\theta\sum_{k\ge1}f^{k}/k$,

$a_n=\sum_{k=1}^{2n-1}k^{-1}\sim\log n$, $\sum f^{k}/k=-\log(1-f)=O(1)$.

Hence

$\hat\theta_W^{obs}=S_{obs}/a_n=\theta\Big[1-\frac{\sum f^{k}/k}{a_n}\Big]\xrightarrow{p}\theta$,

$S_{obs}\xrightarrow{p}S_{true}$ on ${\cal S}_V$. The absolute loss $-\theta\sum f^{k}/k$ is $O(1)$ while $a_n\to\infty$, so the relative bias of Watterson is $O(1)/\log n\to0$. reflection_text.17:
The analysed site set is the union VCF set ${\cal S}_V$. By construction every site in ${\cal S}_V$ is truly segregating pre-filter, $p>0$, and ‘no completely missing SNV across all samples’ is a pre-filter property of the union.

Per haplotype MCAR loss of a true derived call: retention $r=1-f<1$, $f>0$, reference alleles are never lost. After reference fill-in $Y_i=X_i B_i$, $B_i\sim{\rm Bern}(r)$ independent of $X_i$. Hence

$E[\hat p\mid p]=rp<p$,

$E[2\hat p(1-\hat p)\mid p]=2rp[1-rp]<2p(1-p)$ for all $0<p<1$.

So per site heterozygosity is attenuated. In the rare site regime $E[\hat\pi_i]\simeq2rp$.
$E[\hat\pi]=E_p[2rp(1-rp)]<E_p[2p(1-p)]$ and the $r$ thinning persists as $n\to\infty$. $\pi$ is persistently downward biased by missing-as-reference imputation; this is uncontroversial.

Presence/absence. A true site with $k=2np>0$ derived copies is scored segregating after imputation iff $K_o>0$, $K_o|k\sim{\rm Bin}(k,r)$,

$\Pr\{{\rm lost}\mid k\}=f^{k}$, $\Pr\{{\rm segregating}\mid k\}=1-f^{k}$.

For fixed $p>0$, $f^{k}=f^{2np}\to0$ as $n\to\infty$. On infinite sites $E[N_k]=\theta/k$,

$E[S_{obs}]=\sum_{k\ge1}\frac{\theta}{k}[1-f^{k}]
       =\theta a_n-\theta\sum_{k\ge1}f^{k}/k$,

$a_n=\sum_{k=1}^{2n-1}k^{-1}\sim\log n$, $\sum f^{k}/k=-\log(1-f)=O(1)$.

Hence

$\hat\theta_W^{obs}=S_{obs}/a_n=\theta\Big[1-\frac{\sum f^{k}/k}{a_n}\Big]\xrightarrow{p}\theta$,

$S_{obs}\xrightarrow{p}S_{true}$ on ${\cal S}_V$. The absolute loss $-\theta\sum f^{k}/k$ is $O(1)$ while $a_n\to\infty$, so the relative bias of Watterson is $O(1)/\log n\to0$. Up to the common VCF ascertainment to variable sites $\theta_W$ is first-order robust to random allele-independent loss + reference fill-in, whereas the frequency-weighted $\pi$ remains permanently depressed.

Disagreement is about interpretation of ‘arbitrarily large’. Colleagues 1,10,11,12,15,16,17,18 argue the $n\to\infty$ limit is intended: for any fixed $p>0$ $f^{2np}\to0$, so the segregating-site count is asymptotically recovered and only $\pi$ is systematically biased, i.e. B. The $O(1)$ loss $\theta\sum f^{k}/k$ is $o(a_n)$ and vanishes relatively.

Colleagues 13,14,2,5,8,9 argue operationally: the infinite-sites tail supplies infinitely many $k=O(1)$ sites, for which $\Pr\{{\rm loss}\mid k\}=f^{k}>0$ does not depend on $n$. A singleton carried by one haplotype that is filtered is imputed reference/reference in the final alignment even though the site is in the union VCF. Hence $E[S_{obs}]<S_{true}$ for every finite $n$ and $E[\theta_W^{obs}]=\theta[1-(-\log(1-f))/a_n]<\theta$. Both $S$ and $\pi$ are downward biased in expectation, with the usual $O(1)/\log n$ finite-sample bias of $\theta_W$ and persistent $r$ attenuation of $\pi$. That is the both-biased operational conclusion C.

The shared VCF ascertainment to polymorphic sites biases both statistics upward w.r.t. a genome-wide $\theta$, but that bias is common mode and not created by the imputation step.

Current understanding: mathematically, on the ascertained union set $\pi$ is persistently downward biased while $\theta_W$ is asymptotically unbiased, with an $O(1)$ absolute / $O(1)/\log n$ relative finite-sample downward bias. The majority in round 4 restate B as the $n\to\infty$ first-order statement; the C camp keeps the finite-sample $f^{k}>0$ for $k=O(1)$ loss as the operative bias. Unresolved is whether the question intends the formal limit or the operational finite-sample interpretation.
